draft.title: Maslow's hierarchy of needs
card: Abraham Maslow said people have five levels of needs. From the bottom up they are physiological, safety, social, esteem and self-actualisation.
Physiological needs are basics such as food, water and rest. Safety needs include job security and a safe workplace.
Social needs are belonging and friendship. Esteem needs are respect and recognition. Self-actualisation is reaching one's full potential.
Maslow said people move up to the next level once the level below is met. A need that is met no longer motivates, so a manager looks at which level staff are on.
draft.remember: Staff are motivated by the lowest level of need not yet met, then move up.

a.q: Which need is at the very top of Maslow's hierarchy?
opts: Self-actualisation
Esteem
Social
Safety
a.why: Self-actualisation, reaching one's full potential, is the highest level. Esteem is the tempting wrong answer, because it is the level just below and covers respect and recognition.
a.clue: It is about reaching full potential.

b.q: Priya works at a Geelong warehouse on short contracts that may not be renewed. She worries about paying rent. Which offer would best motivate her, by Maslow's theory?
opts: A permanent contract with a steady income
A staff award for the best idea of the month
A place on a team that meets for Friday lunch
A chance to design her own project
b.why: Her worry about income and job security is a safety need, and it is not yet met. Awards and projects target higher levels, so they would motivate her less until safety is met. The Friday lunch is a social need, which sits above safety.
b.clue: Find the lowest level of need she has not yet met.

b.best: A permanent contract with a steady income

problems.detail: The clue 'It is about reaching full potential' repeats the card's definition of self-actualisation word for word. A student can match the clue to the card and pick the answer without knowing the order of the hierarchy.
